title: Preserving the Ancestral Domain
author: Hubert Posadas
description: What does it mean to own land you've lived on for generations — not as property, but as a responsibility? Eleonor V. Atencio walks us through the vision behind a 2-hectare pilot project inside the Dumagat/Remontado ancestral domain in Tanay, Rizal.
about: What does it mean to own land you've lived on for generations — not as property, but as a responsibility? Eleonor V. Atencio walks us through the vision behind a 2-hectare pilot project inside the Dumagat/Remontado ancestral domain in Tanay, Rizal. The project isn't about profit. It's about building a working model that proves ancestral domains can be preserved and made productive at the same time — so communities don't have to sell their land to survive. Topics covered: how the Dumagat/Remontado view land as collective wealth; customary law as a living, oral tradition; the pilot as an immersion ground for partners; and the long-term path toward larger projects within the ancestral domain. Interviewed and facilitated by Sir Hubert Joseph Posadas of the Baganihan Collective.
authorBio: Eleonor V. Atencio is a member of the Dumagat/Remontado ICCs/IPs of Brgy. Cuyambay, Tanay, Rizal. A public-school teacher and IPED Coordinator, she manages Tukduan, the School of Living Traditions of the Dumagat/Remontado. She is President of Tanay Dumagat/Remontado Ancestral Domain Development Inc. (TANAYDRADDEVI) and is completing her Masters in Arts of Education Major in Indigenous Study.

title: An Economist Prepares for the Polycrisis
author: Garbi Jover
description: What does an economist do when the systems he studied start to break down? Garbi Jover left his career and went back to the land. A conversation about the polycrisis and what it means to prepare.
about: What does an economist do when the systems he studied start to break down? Garbi Jover left his career behind and returned to the land. In this conversation, Hubert Joseph Posadas of the Baganihan Collective frames the broader context: the polycrisis, a convergence of ecological collapse, food insecurity, economic instability, and geopolitical tension arriving all at once. Garbi shares the thinking behind his decision, what he learned in the transition, and why communities rooted in land and cooperation are the most resilient response to what is coming. Interviewed and presented by Hubert Joseph Posadas of the Baganihan Collective.
authorBio: Garbi Jover is an economist who chose to step away from conventional financial life to prepare for the polycrisis — a convergence of ecological, economic, and social breakdowns. He now advocates for land-based resilience and community sovereignty as a response to systemic collapse.

title: Exploring the Food Forests of Zaytuna Farm
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Explore the extensive, mature food forests of Zaytuna Farm, a living classroom developed with students over time. This video showcases the dynamic maintenance practices, including pollarding and coppi
about: Explore the extensive, mature food forests of Zaytuna Farm, a living classroom developed with students over time. This video showcases the dynamic maintenance practices, including pollarding and coppicing, used to manage fast-growing support species like ice cream beans and Tipuana tipu. Discover how these "hard-working" plants are strategically utilized for biomass, mulch, and nitrogen fixation, while simultaneously suppressing weeds like Singapore Daisy and fostering a diverse canopy of fruit trees and perennial edibles. Witness the evolution of a food forest from wild abundance to more managed, user-friendly zones, all while maximizing ecological function and food production.
authorBio: Geoff Lawton is a world renowned permaculture consultant, designer and teacher. He first took his Permaculture Design Certificate (PDC) Course in 1983 with Bill Mollison, widely considered the "father of permaculture." Geoff has undertaken thousands of jobs teaching, consulting, designing, administering and implementing, in 6 continents and over 50 countries around the world.

title: Water is the Foundation of Permaculture Design
author: Andrew Millison
description: Water is the foundational element of any permaculture design. This video demonstrates how to begin a permaculture project by first designing for water flow on a site, using a valley landscape as an ex
about: Water is the foundational element of any permaculture design. This video demonstrates how to begin a permaculture project by first designing for water flow on a site, using a valley landscape as an example. Learn how to strategically place ponds, roads, and tree belts to intercept and direct water, creating different zones for various crops and animal systems. Discover how these water-centric structures also facilitate access, nutrient cycling, and even ideal housing locations, all unfolding from the initial water design.
authorBio: Andrew Millison is a permaculture educator and professor at Oregon State University who teaches Introduction to Permaculture — one of the world's most-enrolled online permaculture courses. He is dedicated to spreading practical permaculture knowledge through clear, accessible teaching.

title: How to Compost Simply
author: Morag Gamble
description: Learn how to simplify your composting with a "compost tractor" system that enriches your garden right where you need it. This video demonstrates how to use a standard compost bin to break down kitchen
about: Learn how to simplify your composting with a "compost tractor" system that enriches your garden right where you need it. This video demonstrates how to use a standard compost bin to break down kitchen and garden scraps in situ, creating a vibrant, healthy soil foundation for your plants. Discover the benefits of this method, including reduced pest issues, nutrient-dense food, and improved soil moisture retention, making your gardening efforts easier and more productive.
authorBio: Morag Gamble is an internationally recognised permaculture educator, filmmaker, speaker, and author based in Australia. Founder of Our Permaculture Life and the Permaculture Education Institute, she has been designing and teaching permaculture across the world for over 25 years.

title: Keyline Design: A Regenerative Agriculture Tool
author: Darren Doherty
description: Explore the Australian-born Keyline Design system, a powerful land planning approach focused on water control and soil improvement to create drought-proof and water-secure properties. Learn how Keylin
about: Explore the Australian-born Keyline Design system, a powerful land planning approach focused on water control and soil improvement to create drought-proof and water-secure properties. Learn how Keyline principles guide the strategic placement of trees, roads, ponds, and fences, fostering perennial grasslands and savannas that become enduring carbon sinks. Discover how simple, management-focused techniques like planned holistic grazing form the foundation, with options to integrate tools like keyline plows, biofertilizers, and cocktail cover crops for enhanced results. Witness the dramatic impact of Keyline Design, from restoring barren landscapes to fostering profitable, family-friendly regenerative agriculture.
authorBio: Darren Doherty is one of the world's leading regenerative agriculture designers and the creator of Regrarians, a framework for holistic land design. He has worked across six continents designing landscapes that restore water cycles, build soil, and create productive farm systems.

title: A Secret Technique to Growing Plants from Seed
author: Stefan Sobkowiak
description: Stefan Sobkowiak of Miracle Farms shares a pre-germination seeding technique that dramatically improves germination rates and seedling vigour in permaculture orchards and food forests.
about: Pre-germinating seeds before planting gives seedlings a critical head start — reducing the time they spend vulnerable in the soil and dramatically improving germination rates. Stefan Sobkowiak of Miracle Farms demonstrates his fluid-drilling technique, where seeds are soaked and partially sprouted in a gel medium before being sown directly into prepared beds. The method sidesteps common germination failures caused by soil temperature fluctuations, crust formation, and moisture inconsistency. Applied across a permaculture orchard, this approach results in denser, more uniform stands of plants with far less reseeding required.
authorBio: Stefan Sobkowiak is the founder of Miracle Farms, a commercial permaculture orchard in Quebec, Canada. He applies permaculture design principles to fruit tree cultivation and food forest management, and shares practical growing techniques through The Permaculture Orchard channel.

title: The Farm: Why the Philippines Can’t Feed Itself | Atty. Esteban Salonga with Baganihan Collective
author: Hubert Posadas
description: Hubert Posadas is a Filipino permaculture practitioner and community organizer leading the Bayanihan Project, a program that integrates modern permaculture with indigenous Filipino practices across six pilot communities nationwide. His work is rooted in the belief that food security and community resilience are inseparable, drawing on the Filipino
about: Atty. Esteban Salonga, son of Senator Salonga, shares his journey from contract chicken farming to advocating for a radical shift in Philippine agricultural policy. He critiques the government's focus on export-oriented agriculture and large-scale industries, arguing that this approach neglects the fundamental issue of food security for its own population. Salonga champions a return to sustainable subsistence farming, emphasizing local food production and supporting small-scale farmers and fishermen over global trade interests. He traces the historical roots of this imbalance, from the Green Revolution to the rise of plantation agriculture, and proposes a realignment of priorities to feed the Filipino people first.
authorBio: Hubert Posadas is a Filipino permaculture practitioner and community organizer leading the Bayanihan Project, a program that integrates modern permaculture with indigenous Filipino practices across six pilot communities nationwide. His work is rooted in the belief that food security and community resilience are inseparable, drawing on the Filipino value of bayanihan as the foundation for sustainable land stewardship.

about: This episode of Discover Permaculture explores the fragility of the global food system and how permaculture design offers a resilient alternative to traditional food security. Geoff Lawton and his guests discuss moving beyond anxiety to empowered action by designing self-replicating food systems in your own garden and community. They emphasize the importance of local food production, community collaboration, and creating continuous food abundance through diverse, productive ecosystems, rather than relying on external systems or emergency stockpiling. The conversation highlights the shift from a "prepper" mentality to actively building local food infrastructure and fostering community resilience.

author: Bert Peeters and Sixto Bereber
description: Bert Peeters and Sixto Bereber are permaculture educators and long-time practitioners leading the Philippine Permaculture Association (PPA). Through the Kapitbahay: Kwentong Permakultura series, they share conversations and practical insights on soil health, and community-based permaculture in the Philippine context. Their work focuses on translati
about: This episode of "Kapitbahay: Kwentong Permakultura" delves into the profound importance of soil, exploring its fundamental role beyond just growing plants. Bert and Sixto discuss how healthy soil, rich in organic matter and microorganisms, is the foundation of life, contrasting it with degraded land filled with waste. They highlight the versatility of soil, not only for food production but also as a sustainable building material through techniques like rammed earth, which offers natural climate regulation. The conversation emphasizes the interconnectedness of soil health with human well-being and the broader ecosystem, urging viewers to respect and nurture this vital resource.
authorBio: Bert Peeters and Sixto Bereber are permaculture educators and long-time practitioners leading the Philippine Permaculture Association (PPA). Through the Kapitbahay: Kwentong Permakultura series, they share conversations and practical insights on soil health and community-based permaculture in the Philippine context.

Their work focuses on translati
about: Kapitbahay: Kwentong Permakultura – Episode 1 explores the personal journeys of Bert Peeters and Sixto Bereber into permaculture. Sixto shares how a simple internet search for "odorless pig farming" led him to research permaculture, while Bert recounts his shift from traditional development work to permaculture after realizing the limitations of project-based funding. They discuss the core principles of permaculture, emphasizing ecological relationships, the interconnectedness of natural elements, and the importance of appreciating free resources like rainwater and sunlight. The episode highlights how permaculture fosters empowerment by encouraging individuals to become responsible stewards of their environment and reconnect with Mother Earth, moving away from a convenience-driven lifestyle.
authorBio: Bert Peeters and Sixto Bereber are permaculture educators and long-time practitioners leading the Philippine Permaculture Association (PPA). author: Hubert Posadas
description: Hubert Posadas breaks down the concept of polycrisis. Its what happens when climate, economic, social, and geopolitical crises hit simultaneously and compound on each other. He examines why the Philippines is particularly vulnerable, why the Western model of prepping doesnt translate to the Filipino context, and how bayanihan and indigenous permacu
about: Hubert Posadas breaks down the concept of polycrisis — what happens when climate, economic, social, and geopolitical crises hit simultaneously and compound on each other. He examines why the Philippines is particularly vulnerable, why the Western model of prepping doesn't translate to the Filipino context, and how bayanihan and indigenous permaculture practices offer a solid path to community preparedness.
idealFor: Filipinos wanting to understand how permaculture connects to broader issues of food security, community resilience, and preparing for an increasingly unstable world. Particularly relevant for those interested in the intersection of indigenous practices and practical sustainability.
authorBio: Hubert Posadas is a Filipino permaculture practitioner and community organizer leading the Bayanihan Project, a program that integrates modern permaculture with indigenous Filipino practices across six pilot communities nationwide. His work is rooted in the belief that food security and community resilience are inseparable, drawing on the Filipino value of bayanihan as the foundation for sustainable land stewardship.

title: The Forested Garden: What is a Food Forest?
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton walks through what a food forest actually is and how it works. The video covers the layered structure of a food forest, the role of support species in building soil fertility, how pruning and timing drive productivity, and how animals can be integrated to speed up the whole process. By the end you have a clear picture of how these syst
about: Food forests are designed, productive ecosystems modeled after natural forests, featuring diverse species in multiple layers that provide food with minimal input. This video details the seven layers of a food forest, from canopy to root yield and climbers, and explains how to strategically plant support species alongside productive ones to shelter, fertilize, and condition the soil. It also covers techniques like pollarding and using animals like ducks to accelerate establishment and maintenance, ultimately creating a self-sustaining, high-yielding system.
idealFor: Those looking to understand food forests from the ground up — from the basic concept to the practical management strategies behind a functioning system.

title: Taking the Hard Work Out of Composting!
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Access to high-quality organic fertilizer can be one of the biggest hurdles in growing diverse, healthy crops. In this video, Geoff Lawton introduces the Subpod, a subterranean worm farm designed to turn everyday organic waste into nutrient-rich fertilizer right where it’s needed. The system avoids the usual worm farm problems—no mess, flies, maggo
about: Unlock the secret to abundant organic food production by mastering your own fertilizer supply. This video introduces the Subpod, a subterranean worm farm designed to effortlessly transform kitchen waste into rich organic fertilizer directly in your garden. Discover how this innovative, mess-free system eliminates common composting problems like smells and flies, while simultaneously fertilizing surrounding plants and even serving as a garden seat. Learn how the Subpod's efficient design allows you to convert waste streams into high-quality organic produce in any space, from small gardens to commercial settings. Support the Kickstarter to bring this game-changing composting solution to more gardens.
idealFor: Gardeners, small-scale farmers, and anyone interested in sustainable, zero-waste food production. It shows how simple, well-designed systems can transform kitchen waste into powerful tools for growing healthy, organic crops while reducing energy use and environmental impact.

title: How to Build a Worm Tower
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton is a world renowned permaculture consultant, designer and teacher. He first took his Permaculture Design Certificate (PDC) Course in 1983 with Bill Mollison, widely considered the “father of permaculture.” Geoff has undertaken thousands of jobs teaching, consulting, designing, administering and implementing, in 6 continents and over 50
about: Learn how to build a simple, vertical worm tower that integrates directly into your garden. This design utilizes compost worms to produce nutrient-rich fertilizer and "worm juice" right where your plants need it, offering a convenient and free source of nourishment. Discover how these miniature worm farms provide continuous fertilization without the worms migrating into the surrounding soil. This method is perfect for home, urban, or community gardens seeking an efficient, in-situ composting solution.
authorBio: Geoff Lawton is a world renowned permaculture consultant, designer and teacher. title: Integrated System Design
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Ideal for learners looking to understand the practical mechanics of property design in permaculture. If youre planning your own land project or want to see how water management, access planning, and zoning work together to create a productive, functional system, this video offers the foundational framework to move from concept to implementation wit
about: Geoff Lawton provides a comprehensive walkthrough of integrated system design, focusing on water management, land use, and property productivity. The approach emphasizes working with natural features while integrating engineered solutions like swales, ponds, and windmills to maximize water retention. Central to the design process is the principle of "stop it, spread it, and soak it" — managing water to infiltrate and hydrate soil rather than allowing runoff.
idealFor: Learners looking to understand the practical mechanics of property design in permaculture. If you're planning your own land project or want to see how water management, access planning, and zoning work together to create a productive, functional system, this video offers the foundational framework.
authorBio: Geoff Lawton is a world renowned permaculture consultant, designer and teacher. title: Permaculture Vs Regenerative Agriculture, Syntropic Agriculture & Holistic Management?
author: Geoff Lawton
description: learners trying to understand how permaculture differs from and incorporates other sustainable practices. If youve been confused about where permaculture fits in the broader landscape of regenerative systems, or if youre looking to understand the ethical foundation that distinguishes truly holistic design from scattered techniques, this video provi
about: This video clarifies the relationship between permaculture and other land-use systems like regenerative agriculture, syntropic agriculture, and holistic management. Geoff Lawton explains that permaculture acts as a holistic design science, serving as a "wardrobe" or "toolbox" that ethically organizes and connects various disciplines. He emphasizes that while these other methods are valuable "coat hangers," permaculture provides the overarching framework for integrating them into a comprehensive, ethical design. The discussion highlights permaculture's specialization in connectivity across diverse systems, from land use to urban planning and waste management.
idealFor: Learners trying to understand how permaculture differs from and incorporates other sustainable practices. If you've been confused about where permaculture fits in the broader landscape of regenerative systems, this video provides the conceptual clarity to move forward with confidence.

title: Is It Always Better to Layer Cardboard and Mulch before Planting?
author: Geoff Lawton
description: beginners learning the specific recipes different crops require for successful growth. If youve struggled with carrot germination, wondered when to apply mulch in your garden beds, or want to understand why direct sowing produces better results than transplanting for certain vegetables, this video provides the practical clarity to grow quality carr
about: While layering cardboard and mulch is often a go-to permaculture technique, some crops benefit from a different approach. This video delves into the specific case of carrots, explaining why direct seeding into prepared soil, followed by careful thinning and later mulching, leads to better germination and straighter, healthier roots. It highlights the importance of soil composition, nutrient levels, and strategic timing for delicate seeds, drawing parallels to the developmental stages of a permaculture system. The discussion emphasizes that understanding the unique "recipe" for each crop is key to successful and abundant yields.

title: Water Recycling with Reed Beds
author: Geoff Lawton
description: learners interested in sustainable water management and onsite greywater treatment. If youre looking to understand how to recycle household wastewater for irrigation, reduce freshwater demand, or integrate greywater systems into permaculture designs, this video provides a scalable, cost-effective model that maximizes water and nutrient reuse with m
about: Discover how to transform household greywater into valuable irrigation water using simple, effective reed bed systems. This video showcases three different greywater recycling setups, including a large system for irrigating fruit trees, a kitchen sink system with a grease trap, and a multi-stage system that culminates in a banana circle. Learn the basic principles of horizontal flow reed beds, the importance of grease traps for kitchen greywater, and how to maximize water reuse for productive landscapes. Geoff Lawton demonstrates practical, low-tech solutions for sustainable water management on any scale.

title: How to Make Your Property Fire Resistant with Permaculture Design
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video documents Geoff Lawton’s return to Zaytuna Farm during one of the most severe bushfire seasons in Australia’s history. As record-breaking drought and uncontrollable fires close in on the surrounding region, the film grounds itself in a real, unfolding crisis shaped by climate instability, water scarcity, and prolonged environmental stres
about: Permaculture design offers practical strategies to enhance a property's resilience against bushfires and drought. This video outlines five key techniques, including maximizing rainwater capture and storage in tanks and dams, managing open areas through grazing and mowing, utilizing swales to infiltrate and store water in the soil, and planting fire-resistant tree species as buffers. By implementing these principles, properties can be drought-proofed and significantly increase their fire resistance, reducing the impact of natural disasters.

title: Starting a Permaculture Farm – Step 1: Observe & Interact
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Before anything is built, planted, or altered, permaculture begins with restraint. This first episode of a five-part series focuses on the most overlooked step in starting a permaculture farm: learning how to observe the land before intervening in it. Framed around the first permaculture principle, Observe and Interact, the video lays the groundwor
about: This foundational video for starting a permaculture farm emphasizes the critical "Observe & Interact" principle. It outlines essential pre-design steps, including soil testing for pH and nutrient composition, assessing the water table depth, and comprehensive terrain mapping using tools like drones to understand contours, sun exposure, wind patterns, and existing flora. The goal is to make informed decisions about major installations like ponds or swales, working with nature rather than against it, before committing resources.

title: How to Make a Chicken Composting System
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Chickens can do more than provide eggs—they can become powerful allies in building fertile, productive gardens. This video demonstrates a scalable chicken composting system, showing how chickens’ natural behaviors—scratching, feeding on insects, and consuming weed seeds—can continuously generate nutrient-rich compost while also supporting egg and p
about: Discover how to create a highly efficient chicken composting system that continuously builds fertility for your garden. This design harnesses chickens' natural scratching and consumption habits to transform organic matter into nutrient-dense compost, while also providing eggs and potential meat production. Learn how this system can generate significant volumes of high-quality compost, from a cubic meter per month in a small urban setting to multiple cubic meters weekly for commercial applications. It's a guaranteed-to-work engine of fertility that anyone can implement.

title: How to Build an Instant Garden
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Transforming discarded materials into living soil is at the heart of this video, which walks through the process of sheet mulching—a low-effort method to build fertile, productive garden beds. Using items like old trees, cardboard, paper, manure, and vegetable scraps, the system creates layers that feed worms and countless soil organisms while supp
about: Learn how to create an "instant garden" using the sheet mulching technique, mimicking the forest floor to build rich, fertile soil. This method involves layering organic materials like cardboard, paper, manure, and kitchen scraps directly onto grass, suppressing weeds by cutting out light. Discover how this simple, low-effort system feeds soil organisms, conserves water, moderates soil temperature, and builds up to five centimeters of new soil in a year, ensuring a sustainable and productive garden. See the impressive results of an instant garden after just five weeks, demonstrating how quickly it produces food while simultaneously creating healthy soil.

title: All About Weeds
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton reframes how we think about weeds entirely. Rather than treating them as problems to be eliminated, this video examines what weeds are actually telling you about your soil. Different weeds germinate in response to specific conditions like compaction, nutrient depletion, or post-fire recovery, and understanding that pattern is what sepa
about: Weeds are not just plants in the wrong place, but rather indicators of soil conditions and active participants in ecosystem repair. By observing the types of weeds present, we can "read the landscape" to understand issues like compaction, loose soil, or nutrient deficiencies (potassium, nitrogen). Geoff Lawton demonstrates how specific weeds, like dandelions or bracken fern, reveal underlying problems and how their natural functions can be harnessed to restore soil health and accelerate ecological succession towards abundant, productive systems. Understanding weeds without prejudice allows us to work with nature's repair mechanisms, even suggesting "designer weeds" or cover crops to outcompete unruly weeds and fertilize the soil.

title: How to Make and Maintain Soil Fertility
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton walks through how to get serious productivity out of a small garden space. The video covers dense layered planting, on-site composting using simple cage systems, companion planting for natural pest management, and how integrating chickens creates a closed-loop fertility cycle. It shows exactly how these systems are built and maintained
about: This video demonstrates how to create and maintain soil fertility in an intensive small-space garden, focusing on diverse planting strategies that mimic a forest floor. It details a simple, rapid composting method using layered brown, green, and manure materials, with a specific turning schedule for quick results. Additionally, the video showcases an "urban chicken tractor" deep litter system, explaining how it efficiently produces nutrient-rich compost every two weeks for continuous garden fertilization.

title: Compost Worm Farming
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton breaks down how to build a home worm farm system using something as simple as an old bathtub. The video covers the difference between compost worms and regular earthworms, what to feed them, how the three month harvest cycle works, and how to get both liquid and solid fertilizer out of the same system. Its a genuinely low cost, low mai
about: Learn how to build a simple, effective worm farm using an old bathtub to transform kitchen scraps into nutrient-rich liquid and solid fertilizers. This guide details the ideal conditions for compost worms, including their preferred diet (excluding citrus and onions) and the importance of proper drainage and layering. Discover how to harvest your worm castings and "juice" every three months, ensuring a continuous supply of high-quality, bacteria-rich fertilizer for your organic garden. This method helps close the waste stream loop of your food system, promoting sustainable and productive gardening.

title: Connecting Science, Ethics, and Climate with Permaculture Design
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video takes a step back from the practical side of permaculture and examines what the discipline actually is at its core. The speaker covers permaculture as a connecting framework between different fields rather than a standalone expertise, why ethics and science form its foundation, how climate literacy shapes every design decision, and where
about: Permaculture is a connecting system between disciplines, not a collection of isolated subjects. Geoff Lawton emphasizes the importance of understanding core scientific principles, especially climate data, and grounding all design in ethics. He cautions against unproven sciences and highlights the potential dangers of unchecked technological advancements, stressing the need for a sensible, proven approach to design. Ultimately, the goal of a permaculture teacher is to empower students to become better designers and consultants, fostering a deeper understanding of the interconnectedness of science, ethics, and climate.

title: What is a Mainframe in Permaculture?
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton walks through the mainframe approach to landscape design  a hierarchical framework that starts with water, then access routes, then structures. The video explains why the order matters, how water patterns should inform every subsequent decision, and how designing access along contour lines doubles as passive water harvesting infrastruc
about: This video introduces the concept of "mainframe" design in permaculture, emphasizing the importance of carefully considered, long-term planning before implementing smaller elements. It outlines a hierarchical approach to design, prioritizing water first, then access, and finally structural positions. The discussion delves into the multifaceted nature of water, its patterns, and how to integrate it into a landscape, along with strategies for designing multi-functional access that cooperates with water harvesting. Ultimately, understanding these mainframe patterns provides a robust foundation for creating abundant, diverse, and resilient permaculture systems.

title: Why Do We Focus on Legumes for Nitrogen-Fixing?
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton gets into the specifics of nitrogen fixation  how it actually works, which legumes do it, which ones dont, and why inoculation with rhizobium bacteria makes the difference between a cover crop that builds your soil and one that doesnt. The video covers practical identification of nitrogen-fixing nodules on roots, how to source and appl
about: This video delves into the world of nitrogen-fixing plants, primarily focusing on legumes due to their prevalence and effectiveness. Geoff Lawton explains which legumes reliably fix nitrogen, whether inoculation is necessary, and how to identify nitrogen nodules on plant roots. He also demonstrates practical applications, such as using cover crops like cowpea and vetch, and shares a historical anecdote about traditional inoculation methods. The video provides valuable insights for permaculturists looking to enhance soil fertility naturally.

title: Yields, Surpluses, Overabundance, and Resource Consumption within a System
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video reframes how we think about yield in ecological systems. Rather than measuring output against what you put in, it examines yield as a function of how well a system captures and converts solar energy. The core argument is that diversity alone isnt enough  its the connectivity and interaction between elements that determines how productive
about: This video explores the fundamental relationship between yields, surpluses, and resource consumption in a permaculture system. It emphasizes how truly sustainable systems ideally produce resources rather than consume them, all stemming from efficient solar energy capture through photosynthesis. Geoff Lawton explains that by creating life-rich, diverse, and interconnected systems, we can significantly reduce external inputs and generate abundant onsite resources, moving towards genuine self-sufficiency.

title: How to Transition From Industrialized Agriculture to Permaculture?
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video makes a direct case for why industrial agriculture is failing and how permaculture and urban food systems could replace it faster than most people assume. The speaker backs the argument with concrete numbers  land use efficiency, yield per acre, nutrient density comparisons  and argues that the transition isnt about sacrifice but about p
about: This video directly challenges the necessity and efficacy of industrial agriculture, arguing that a global transition to permaculture could be achieved rapidly—within six months—with only benefits and no sacrifice. It highlights the superior nutrient density, diversity, and ecological repair offered by urban and perimeter urban agriculture, which can produce hundreds of times more food per square meter than industrial systems. The discussion emphasizes that permaculture systems, utilizing only 4-6% of the land currently used by industrial agriculture, can provide meaningful employment, better nutrition, and improved psychological well-being, ultimately advocating for the immediate and conscious abandonment of destructive industrial practices.

title: Design it or Leave it Alone? Geoff on Ethical Design & Regrowth
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton tackles a question that doesnt get asked enough in permaculture  when is it actually ethical to intervene in land thats already recovering on its own? The video examines how to read the quality and stage of forest regrowth, why non-native pioneer species deserve more respect than they get, and where the line is between responsible deve
about: This video explores the ethical considerations of designing permaculture systems on disturbed land, particularly focusing on the balance between human intervention and natural succession. Geoff Lawton outlines a "breakpoint" for intervention based on the age and quality of regrowth forest, advocating for working with low-quality, younger regrowth or open land over established, high-quality ecosystems. He also highlights the valuable role of "hardworking immigrant" species in initial landscape recovery and how to leverage these novel ecosystems to accelerate desired succession. The discussion emphasizes learning from natural processes to make informed choices about land management.

title: 11 Amazing Mulch Materials for Permaculture Gardening
author: Geoff Lawton
description: A straightforward rundown of 11 natural mulching materials and how each one performs in a permaculture context. The video covers everything from wood chip and comfrey to seaweed and sheeps wool, explaining the specific conditions each mulch suits best, how they affect soil biology, and why choosing locally available materials over imported ones is
about: Discover 11 natural and effective mulch materials for your permaculture garden, from readily available sheep's wool and wood chips to nutrient-rich comfrey and animal manure. Learn how different mulches like ramial chipped wood and grass clippings can benefit both annuals and perennials by retaining moisture, suppressing weeds, and building healthy soil. Explore strategies for utilizing local resources like seaweed or even existing plant matter through chop-and-drop techniques to enhance your garden's fertility and resilience.

title: Elements vs. Functions in Permaculture
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video breaks down one of the most fundamental concepts in permaculture design  the relationship between elements and their functions. Using a real working example of a gravity-fed water system that connects a dam, pipe, tap, kitchen garden, and cattle trough, it shows how every component in a well-designed system serves a deliberate purpose an
about: Geoff Lawton clarifies the fundamental permaculture concepts of elements and functions, explaining that an element is a component of a design, while its function is what it does within the system. Using examples from his own farm, he illustrates how a tap is an element whose function is to deliver gravity-fed water, and a dam is an element that stores water. He further demonstrates this by detailing the role of a male papaya tree, an element that, despite not fruiting much, serves the vital function of pollinating female trees to produce fertile seeds. This integrated approach highlights how every component in a permaculture design serves a valuable purpose, contributing to the overall efficiency and productivity of the system.

title: Permaculture Demystified: Your Essential Guide for Beginner Green Thumbs!
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Billy from Perma Pastures Farm walks through a real working example of integrated animal management  sheep, chickens, and bees operating as a single coordinated system. The sheep graze down vegetation around the bee boxes, the chickens follow to handle insects and mites that would otherwise threaten the colony, and the bees pollinate the whole oper
about: This video offers a practical, real-world demonstration of permaculture principles in action, specifically focusing on integrated pest and weed management around beehives. Viewers will learn how to utilize a rotational grazing system with sheep to clear tall weeds, followed by chickens to control beetles and mites, all while minimizing human labor. The creator illustrates the symbiotic relationships between different elements of a farm ecosystem, emphasizing how each component plays a vital role in improving the land and supporting overall health. This hands-on example provides a clear and concise understanding of permaculture as a collaborative, interconnected system.
idealFor: Those who find permaculture easier to grasp through real examples than through theory. If you've heard the principles but want to see them working together on an actual farm, this is a good place to start.
authorBio: Geoff Lawton is a world renowned permaculture consultant, designer and teacher. He first took his Permaculture Design Certificate (PDC) Course in 1983 with Bill Mollison, widely considered the "father of permaculture." Geoff has undertaken thousands of jobs teaching, consulting, designing, administering and implementing, in 6 continents and over 50 countries around the world.

title: Permaculture Soils Perspective
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Jacob Kollen, a soil scientist with a permaculture background, breaks down what soil actually is and why pore space matters as much as the solid material itself. The video walks through how climate drives weathering, how dryland, temperate, and tropical soils differ in structure and behavior, and why those differences demand completely different ag
about: Explore the fundamental role of "space" in soil function, from its ability to support life to its capacity for water and nutrient retention. This presentation delves into the process of weathering, explaining how climate, organisms, relief, parent material, and time influence soil particle size and structure. Discover how soil characteristics vary across dryland, temperate, and tropical climates, and learn about landscape position's impact on agricultural strategies.

title: Before You Create Permaculture Swales, Watch this Swale Guide and Example!
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video covers swales from the ground up  what they actually are in a permaculture context versus how conventional landscaping uses the term, how to construct them correctly, and why trees on the berm arent optional. The presenter walks through how swale dimensions should be adapted to soil type, slope, and rainfall, uses his own site in Central
about: This comprehensive guide demystifies permaculture swales, differentiating them from conventional drainage ditches and emphasizing their role in water infiltration and groundwater recharge. It details the construction process, from measuring ground level with an A-frame to the importance of uncompacted bottoms and berms, and explores how to adapt swale design (size, depth, and amendments) to various climates, soil types, and rainfall patterns. The video also highlights the critical role of trees planted on swale berms for evapotranspiration and offers practical advice on when and where swales are most effective, including a real-world example from a central Italian site.

title: The 12 Myths of Permaculture | Setting The Record Straight
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video works through 12 of the most common misconceptions about permaculture  that its only for rural land, only for experts, only for warm climates, too expensive, too complicated, or only about growing food. Each myth gets a direct, practical rebuttal. Its a good reset for anyone whos picked up assumptions about what permaculture is or isnt b
about: This video debunks twelve common misconceptions about permaculture, offering a clear and practical understanding of its core principles. It addresses myths such as permaculture being solely for rural properties, expensive, a new concept, or only for growing food. The discussion emphasizes permaculture's universality, cost-effectiveness, deep historical roots in indigenous wisdom, and holistic design approach applicable to any climate or scale. By clarifying these misunderstandings, the video aims to make permaculture more accessible and less intimidating for beginners.

title: A comprehensive guide to Permaculture Guilds
author: Geoff Lawton
description: The presenter covers soil building, nitrogen fixation, nutrient accumulation, pollinator attraction, and pest deterrence, then walks through six real guilds on his own property showing how those functions play out in practice. The emphasis throughout is on adapting to your specific conditions and letting the system evolve through observation rather
about: This comprehensive guide demystifies permaculture guilds, explaining them not as rigid plant combinations but as human attempts to mimic nature's dense, diverse polycultures. It emphasizes understanding plant functions over exact replication, particularly for cold-hardy, cold-climate fruit tree guilds. The video details essential guild functions, including soil building through ground cover, nutrient cycling with deep tap-rooted accumulators, and nitrogen fixation, all aimed at creating resilient, productive ecosystems.

title: PERMACULTURE PONDS: Why, Where & How
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video walks through the full scope of pond design in permaculture  the different types of ponds and what each one is actually built to do, how landscape position and soil type determine where a pond should go, and the engineering fundamentals behind dam construction, water outlets, and spillways. Its not a beginner overview  it gets into the d
about:
PERMACULTURE PONDS: Why, Where & How

This video explores the diverse purposes and strategic placement of permaculture ponds, from seepage ponds that recharge aquifers to irrigation, recreation, firefighting, habitat, and aquaculture ponds. It details the unique design considerations for each type, emphasizing the importance of understanding soil types, water sources, and potential multi-functional uses. The discussion also delves into the critical decision of placing ponds either in-channel or off-channel, weighing the benefits and liabilities of each approach regarding water flow, storage efficiency, and regulatory considerations. Ultimately, the video guides viewers through the complex thought process of designing a resilient and beneficial water body within a permaculture landscape.

description: This mini-documentary zooms in on a particular project, which involves restoration through Permaculture, to represent the broader and vaster environmental issues taking storm in our world today. It begins by addressing the problematic situations plaguing our modern world (climate change, water and food scarcity), but then it immediately transports
about: This webinar, led by Melanie Stock, an urban and small firm extension specialist for Utah State, delves into the critical role of soil organic matter for garden health. Stock, a soil scientist, emphasizes two key "Garden C's": compost and cover crops, as primary methods for increasing organic matter. She discusses the natural organic matter levels in Utah soils compared to other regions and outlines the numerous benefits of healthy soil, including improved structure, nutrient retention, and water infiltration. The presentation also touches on various materials that can be added to soil to boost organic matter, such as plant residues, mulches, and even some wood products, while cautioning against the use of wood ash in Utah.

author: Geoff Lawton

about: Starting a permaculture garden or farm can feel overwhelming, but this video breaks down five essential first steps. Learn how to observe your land, assess your personal needs and goals, set a realistic budget of time and money, and create a detailed site map to guide your design. These practical tips emphasize slow, small solutions, empowering you to begin your permaculture journey without needing to be an expert or make large, irreversible changes.

Explore principles like designing from patterns to details, integrating rather than segregating, and creatively responding to change to build resilient and productive systems.

about: This video challenges the concept of "waste," demonstrating how everyday discards can be transformed into valuable resources. It showcases practical permaculture techniques for converting rainwater, fallen leaves, humanure, and even gray water from laundry and showers into fertile soil, irrigation for edible plants, and shade-providing infrastructure. By highlighting examples like salvaged metal awnings, repurposed chicken waterers, and street-side water harvesting basins, the video inspires viewers to see potential in what is often thrown away, ultimately improving quality of life and community resilience.

title: Where to Begin When Evolving a Piece of Land into a Permaculture Site
author: Geoff Lawton
description: This video introduces one of the most important principles in permaculture design: starting with observation and planning before taking action on the land. The speaker explains why beginners often feel overwhelmed when beginning a permaculture project and why rushing into planting or earthworks can lead to costly mistakes.
about: Starting a permaculture evolution on a piece of land can feel overwhelming, but the key is to prioritize observation and foundational elements before diving into species selection. This video emphasizes a "water, access, structures" mantra for initial design: first analyze water possibilities across the site to slow, spread, and soak it, then harmonize access with the water pattern for long-term efficiency, and finally, determine structural positions based on these established elements. This methodical approach ensures a robust and sustainable permaculture design, making life easier for both the land and its steward.

about: This video illustrates the stark differences between traditional and permaculture landscape design through a compelling narrative. It compares two design approaches for a young family seeking self-sufficiency and health, highlighting how permaculture integrates elements like chicken coops, greenhouses, and food forests into a cohesive, low-input, and highly productive system. The permaculture design emphasizes passive water harvesting, natural fertilization, and even home heating/cooling, ultimately creating an abundance that can be shared with the community. It showcases how thoughtful, interconnected design can lead to a more sustainable and resilient lifestyle.

title: Reading the Landscape with Permaculture Design
author: Geoff Lawton

about: Geoff Lawton explains how to "read" the landscape by identifying key geological features that reveal a region's climate and water dynamics. He emphasizes the distinction between rounded, humid landscapes and angular, arid ones, detailing how to locate the "key point" at the top of every valley where convex surfaces transition to concave. This crucial point, central to P.A. Yeomans' Keyline farming, represents the highest location to hold water and is a fundamental planning point for sustainable design. Understanding these landscape profiles allows for effective water management and informed permaculture design, fostering a deeper connection to planetary systems.

title: Mapping in Permaculture
author: Geoff Lawton
description: Geoff Lawton explains how mapping is one of the most important first steps in permaculture design. Before planting trees or building systems, a designer must understand the landscape itself. Permaculture works by studying real patterns in nature and using them to guide sustainable land use. By analyzing a site’s location, altitude, climate influenc
about: Mapping is an essential first step in permaculture design, allowing designers to understand a site's unique characteristics and patterns. This video details how to gather foundational data using LIDAR, satellite imagery, or drone flights to create digital maps that depict physical objects, elevation, and crucial slope gradients. These detailed maps enable informed decisions for ideal placement of homes, gardens, forests, and grazing areas, promoting cycles of abundance and long-term fertility. The principles extend beyond individual properties, demonstrating how mapping entire catchments can foster community-wide understanding for land restoration and a stable, productive ecology.

about: Join Geoff Lawton as he visits a burgeoning food garden project in the subtropics of Cape Byron, Australia, spearheaded by Dave Rastovich and his wife, Lauren. Witness the initial stages of transforming a neglected landscape into a productive, community-focused food system designed to feed eight local families. Discover how permaculture principles, including earthworks that harmonize with the land's natural contours and strategic water harvesting, are being implemented to localize food production, improve community health, and regenerate the ecology of a twice-logged and burnt site. The video highlights the practical application of Lidar and satellite GIS technology in designing contour garden beds and footpaths, demonstrating how to work with natural patterns to reduce labor and maximize yield.

It details how to observe and map your site's sectors and internal factors, with a particular focus on designing for water through earthworks like swales or alternative strategies like hugelkultur berms and compost-filled paths. The creator also highlights the importance of building healthy soil and strategically capturing rainwater and gray water to create a resilient and abundant system.

It details the use of various roof types, gutter systems, and a simple first flush mechanism to clean water before it enters storage tanks. The video also explores different tank sizes and their ideal uses, as well as methods for maintaining water pressure and filtering water at its point of use.

title: What is Permaculture?
author: Geoff Lawton

about: Permaculture is introduced as the world's first system of conscious functional design, aiming to create sustainable systems that produce more energy than they consume. Geoff Lawton explains its origins in the 1970s, questioning why agriculture deviates from nature's perennial dominance. He defines permaculture as a persistent system supporting human existence, emphasizing integrated design that minimizes work and pollution by ensuring every system component's needs are met. The core idea is to design in harmony with nature, allowing it to enhance and guide the system for sustainable land use and living.
